title: Unit 9 · Abilities and experiences
description: Saber and poder, practical skills, personal qualities, neither/nor, and introductory life experiences.
source: Original exercises aligned to the Aula Internacional Plus 1 Unit 9 syllabus; no textbook exercise text copied.

cards.translation: I know how to drive.
cards.note: Saber + infinitive expresses knowing how to do something.

cards.translation: Do you know how to swim?
cards.note: Sabes is the tú form of saber.

cards.translation: She knows how to cook very well.
cards.note: Sabe is the third-person singular of saber.

cards.translation: We know how to dance salsa.
cards.note: Sabemos is the nosotros form of saber.

cards.translation: They know how to speak French.
cards.note: Saben is the ellos form of saber.

cards.translation: Today I cannot go to class.
cards.note: Poder changes o to ue: puedo.

cards.translation: Can you help me?
cards.note: Puedes is the tú form of poder.

cards.translation: May I come in?
cards.note: ¿Puedo...? is a common way to ask permission.

cards.translation: We can meet tomorrow.
cards.note: The stem does not change in the nosotros form.

cards.translation: They cannot work today.
cards.note: Pueden is the ellos form of poder.

cards.translation: I know your sister.
cards.note: Use conocer for knowing a person; the yo form is conozco.

cards.translation: I do not know the answer.
cards.note: Use saber for knowing information.

cards.translation: My friend plays the guitar.
cards.note: Tocar un instrumento means to play an instrument.

cards.translation: Do you know how to play the piano?
cards.note: Use tocar for playing a musical instrument.

cards.translation: I know how to take good photos.
cards.note: Hacer fotos means to take photos.

cards.translation: My grandfather knows how to use the computer.
cards.note: Ordenador is common in Spain; computador or computadora is common in Latin America.

cards.translation: I know how to ride a bicycle.
cards.note: Montar en bicicleta means to ride a bicycle.

cards.prompt: No sé ___. Nunca voy a la nieve.
cards.translation: I don't know how to ski. I never go to the snow.
cards.note: Esquiar means to ski.

cards.translation: She sings very well.
cards.note: Bien is an adverb and does not change for gender.

cards.translation: My son knows how to draw animals.
cards.note: Dibujar means to draw.

cards.prompt: Ana siempre tiene un plan; es muy ___.
cards.translation: Ana always has a plan; she is very organized.
cards.note: Organizada agrees with Ana.

cards.translation: Pedro loses everything; he is absent-minded.
cards.note: Despistado means absent-minded or forgetful.

cards.translation: Lucía never gets angry; she is patient.
cards.note: Paciente has the same singular form for men and women.

cards.prompt: Carlos habla con todo el mundo; es ___.
cards.translation: Carlos talks to everyone; he is sociable.
cards.note: Sociable has the same form for masculine and feminine.

cards.prompt: Marta habla poco con desconocidos; es ___.
cards.translation: Marta speaks little with strangers; she is shy.
cards.note: Tímida agrees with Marta.

cards.translation: My classmates study a lot; they are hardworking.
cards.note: The adjective must agree with the group.

cards.prompt: Ella siempre tiene ideas nuevas; es muy ___.
cards.translation: She always has new ideas; she is very creative.
cards.note: Creativa agrees with ella.

cards.prompt: Siempre llega a tiempo; es una persona ___.
cards.translation: He or she always arrives on time; this is a responsible person.
cards.note: Responsable has the same form for masculine and feminine.

cards.prompt: No toca la guitarra ___ el piano.
cards.translation: He plays neither the guitar nor the piano.
cards.note: No... ni... means neither... nor....

cards.translation: I can neither sing nor dance.
cards.note: Ni connects two negative alternatives.

cards.translation: She knows how to run and also knows how to swim.
cards.note: También adds another affirmative idea.

cards.prompt: No sé conducir y mi hermano ___.
cards.translation: I cannot drive and neither can my brother.
cards.note: Tampoco adds another negative idea.

cards.translation: I have traveled to Mexico twice.
cards.note: The present perfect uses he + past participle for a past experience connected to now.

cards.translation: I have lived in three cities.
cards.note: The past participle of vivir is vivido.

cards.translation: I have never eaten paella.
cards.note: The past participle of comer is comido.

cards.translation: Have you seen this film?
cards.note: Visto is the irregular past participle of ver.

cards.translation: Have you ever been to Chile?
cards.note: Estar forms the participle estado.

cards.translation: I have never flown on an airplane.
cards.note: The past participle of volar is volado.

cards.translation: I have already finished the course.
cards.note: Ya often accompanies the present perfect to mean already.

cards.translation: I have not read the book yet.
cards.note: Todavía no means not yet; leído is the participle of leer.

cards.translation: I am looking for a roommate.
cards.note: Un compañero de piso is a flatmate or roommate.

cards.translation: I want to share a flat with another person.
cards.note: Compartir means to share.
